name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd
title: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd - 532540 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 CC revenue +0.5% QoQ with margin flat at 24% as subcontracting and bench build absorb AI-era investment; no numeric guidance, management only says it will "inch up" margins, with MHP ~50bps headwind.

triggers.label: Subcon and bench build ahead of demand
triggers.quote: we have invested in a higher bench and increased hiring of subcontractors to meet near-term skills and delivery requirements

triggers.label: Margin 25% exit target softened to 'inch up'
triggers.quote: we'll try to balance with operating levers. While it's an uphill task, we'll continue to endeavor to inch up on our margins.

triggers.label: India revenue deferral, client count drop
triggers.quote: In India, we had a project deferral, which caused this revenue decrease.

triggers.label: AI pricing better, rev/employee slightly lower
triggers.quote: we are seeing better pricing on the AI revenues we are generating. And if you take the revenue per employee, you will see there's a slight reduction

guidance.quote: we'd look towards inching up from where we are, whilst not losing sight of prioritizing investments for growth.
we are going to keep it at 26%-28%. And that's the long-term aspiration we'll work towards.

summary.headline: TCS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 0.5% QoQ in constant currency to ₹73,188 crore; operating margin held at 24% amid higher subcontracting and investments.
summary.overview: Constant-currency revenue grew 0.5% QoQ and 2.8% YoY, with international up 1.2% QoQ and India up 6% QoQ, though Regional Markets fell on an India project deferral. Growth broadened across BFSI, Manufacturing and Technology & Services, while Consumer and ERU declined. Operating margin was stable at 24% and net margin 19%, with management prioritising investment (higher bench, subcontractors, partnerships, M&A) over near-term margin expansion. Annualised AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion, over 10% of revenue, and TCV was $9.6 billion excluding Porsche and Best Buy deals.

financial_highlights.value: US$9.6 billion (excludes Porsche and Best Buy deals)

financial_highlights.change: AI revenue grew ~19% per analyst question, not disputed

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Largest large vertical and biggest growth contributor: +2.5% QoQ and +3.9% YoY in constant currency, broad-based across banking, capital markets and insurance.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.2% YoY; demand improving in factory automation, engineering productivity, and industrial AI.

segments.name: Technology and Services
segments.commentary: +3.1% QoQ and +4.8% YoY, driven by enterprise software, cloud modernisation and digital transformation; traditional app and infra portfolios seeing agentic AI adoption.

segments.name: Consumer Business
segments.commentary: -0.7% QoQ and -1% YoY; retail and consumer products hit by inflation, energy costs and insourcing, though QoQ decline improved versus prior quarter.

segments.name: Life Sciences and Healthcare
segments.commentary: +0.3% QoQ, stable demand from compliance, clinical/research platforms and AI-enabled drug discovery.

segments.name: Communications and Media
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ; media and digital platforms offset by continued telecom pressure.

segments.name: Energy, Resources and Utilities
segments.commentary: -0.5% QoQ; management sees medium-term structural recovery.

segments.name: Regional Markets / India
segments.commentary: India revenue grew 6% QoQ, while Regional Markets grew 3.6% YoY; management cited a project deferral in India (not hardware pass-through) that reduced Regional Markets revenue, expected to return in medium term.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance; management expects medium-term growth momentum to continue based on TCV, pipeline and client conversations.
Long-term EBIT margin aspiration unchanged at 26%-28%; near-term priority remains investment, so management says it will 'inch up' from 24% rather than commit to 25% exit.
H2 headwinds flagged: MHP acquisition dilution of about 50 bps (timing-dependent), normal furlough seasonality and continued ecosystem investments.
Q3 furlough expected to be similar to prior years; BSNL deal expected to provide cushion for next couple of quarters.
North America expected to recover and become healthy soon; Consumer expected to improve medium term, with Q3 seasonally important.
Data center business: capacity to be built after contracts are signed; revenue expected 18-24 months after start.
capex_capacity: Higher bench and subcontractor usage to meet near-term new-age skill demand; hiring lags deployment for new skills.
Acquisition of MHP (Porsche-linked mobility engineering) subject to regulatory approvals; Best Buy GCC engagement announced.
Data center expansion will be planned once contracts are won; revenue 18-24 months after capacity build starts.
Launched Autonomous Engineering Lab powered by NVIDIA in Bengaluru and an AI-first lights-out factory lab in Pune.
Expanding into data center services, GCC and mid-market offerings, ServiceNow, Public Services and Sovereign Cloud.
demand_pricing: Demand environment not materially changed QoQ; discretionary programs without near-term value remain under scrutiny.
Three AI demand patterns: AI-native outcome solutions, AI-led enterprise systems transformation, and autonomous GBS; AI governance and secure platforms becoming a top need.
Pricing: management said AI revenue is priced better, revenue per employee slightly lower, and overall portfolio pricing broadly stable.
Subcontracting rose across India and overseas; only partly linked to visa fee hike.
Win rates improved; growth attributed partly to vendor consolidation in traditional services.

qa_highlights.question: Will the international growth momentum continue in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not comment on the next quarter but is confident of medium-term growth based on TCV, pipeline and client conversations.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the India revenue decline and client-count drop?
qa_highlights.answer: A project deferral in India caused the decline, expected to return in later quarters; the client drop below the $100 million band was a single account pushed below the threshold by currency movement.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin levers toward 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir Seksaria cited subcontracting cost reduction, investments starting to deliver, productivity, utilisation and non-employee expense control; long-term aspiration stays at 26%-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline QoQ, and what is the margin path to exit FY27 at 25%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin decline reflects higher subcontractor and third-party expenses; H2 headwinds include ~50 bps MHP dilution, so management will only aim to inch margins up.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI revenues margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: The $3.1 billion annualised AI revenue comes in at a much higher margin than the company average.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40% YoY growth in delivery-related costs an upfront investment that will pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Samir said it is a combination of investment in capacity ahead of growth and partnership costs; subcontracting is an optimisation lever, and fees to external consultants carry incremental delivery cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America lagging, and how will Consumer and ERU play out in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects North America to recover soon based on TCV and client conversations; Consumer expected to improve medium term, ERU to recover structurally over medium term.

risks_watch: Margin: investments and subcontracting keep gross margin under pressure; MHP dilution ~50 bps in H2 and BSNL timing uncertain.
Regional Markets volatility from lumpy deliveries; India deferral revenue expected back but no date given.
AI deflation from productivity gains may offset AI-led growth in BFSI and Hi-Tech; management would not call it complete.
Consumer and ERU continue to decline; telecom remains under pressure.
Discretionary spend and North America recovery timing remain uncertain.
Bench and hiring ahead of demand; conversion of new-skill capacity into revenue needs to show in coming quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI, TCV and medium-term growth, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, which management says will remain under investment pressure. Answers on India deferral and client-count drop were reassuring but gave no firm timing.
key_quotes: Annualized AI revenue reached $3.1 billion and crossed 10% of our overall revenue.
Overall, our long-term aspiration remains unchanged, continues to be 26% to 28%.
So, there is no structural issue, and we are hoping to deliver these projects in subsequent quarters once the projects are reinstated.
And we expect North America revenue to recover and become healthy soon.

adds.what: Data centre capacity (MW), to be built only after contracts are signed; revenue 18-24 months after build starts
MHP (Porsche-linked mobility engineering) acquisition, subject to regulatory approvals; adds revenue via M&A, not own capacity

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management expects medium-term growth based on TCV ($9.6B ex-Porsche/Best Buy), pipeline and conversations, with H2 headwinds (about 50 bps MHP dilution, furlough seasonality) and margin only to 'inch up' from 24%, so growth backing is vague.
